candidate.background_need: Vocational teams in Finland and Sweden currently teach similar repair skills separately. There is a development gap regarding the lack of shared learning opportunities between these regions.

objectives.description: Establish a jointly designed repair module that both Finnish and Swedish teams can deliver.
Enable participants to identify specific knowledge gaps in their own practice through cross-border comparison.

preliminary_activities.description: Co-design a shared repair module curriculum with representatives from both Finnish and Swedish teams.
Conduct joint teaching sessions where each team observes the other's delivery of the co-designed module.

expected_results.description: Completion of a jointly designed repair module curriculum document.
Documented feedback on teaching methods from at least 5 participants per country.

proposed_indicators.description: Number of co-designed module pages finalized.
Percentage of participants reporting at least one new teaching technique observed in the other country (Target: 60%).
proposed_indicators.measurement_method: Post-session survey using Likert scale and open text analysis.

assumptions: Both participating teams have sufficient time allocated for the proposed joint activities.
There is a baseline level of technical compatibility between the Finnish and Swedish vocational standards.
Language barriers can be managed through existing translation resources or bilingual facilitators.
open_questions: What specific regulatory differences exist that might hinder the formal recognition of learning outcomes?
Are there sufficient funding mechanisms within an Interreg-style framework to support this pilot without additional grants?
How can language support be effectively integrated into a twelve-month schedule for adult learners?

Experimental prompt version: structured_planning_A_v1
Generate a useful early ConceptPaper. Explain the specific development gap and its consequences using supplied evidence; state what evidence is missing. Distinguish direct participants from wider beneficiaries. Set at most two achievable participant/organisational change objectives and four feasible sequenced activities linked to them. Distinguish tangible outputs, observable results and longer-term impacts; do not promise unsupported impact attribution. Use at most three results and three indicators. Each indicator must define its unit, unique counting rule or percentage numerator/denominator, assessment criterion, collection method and assessment timing. For qualitative change propose an appropriate observation/reflection method without claiming clinical effects. If baseline, targets, capacity or duration are missing, label proposed choices as provisional and ask concise questions instead of inventing facts. Record up to three material feasibility assumptions/risks in assumptions and up to three high-priority open questions. Work packages/roles/budget are not fields in ConceptPaper; do not add schema keys or pretend this is a complete application. Keep the concept concise but substantive.
